observations.behavior: Replaces a regex with one using possessive matching and atomic groups; this prevents catastrophic backtracking on inputs containing many opening brackets.
observations.posthog_connection: Changes shared Markdown sanitization used by Slack and other destinations to stop potential DoS or performance degradation from malformed input.

observations.behavior: Adds regression tests including the specific case of 32,000 leading brackets that previously caused three-second execution times.
observations.posthog_connection: Provides evidence that the implementation resolves the identified performance risk rather than leaving it untested.

observations.limitations: Only P1 is supplied. No changes are shown for callers, configuration, or broader deployment context. The tier relies solely on the local fix and its test without seeing wider adoption or systemic integration.

review.reason: The patch demonstrates a substantive bounded improvement: replacing an unsafe regex pattern and adding targeted performance regression tests. This addresses reliability and availability risks in shared markdown processing but does not show broader architectural change or multi-component benefit.
review.posthog_relevance: Shared helper could protect downstream consumers (Slack, warehouse ingestion) from denial-of-service behavior triggered by maliciously crafted messages; this matters regardless of current volume.
review.uncertainty: Without access to other hunks, we cannot assess whether additional safeguards, rollout strategy, or dependent components were also changed.
